statement: Lenalidomide pharmacokinetics are linear: Cmax and AUC increase in proportion to dose over at least 5 to 400 mg, in healthy volunteers and patients.

primary_source.title: Withdrawal assessment report for Lenalidomide Celgene Europe
primary_source.location: PDF page 20, 'Dose proportionality and time dependencies'
quotes: The pharmacokinetic disposition of lenalidomide is linear in healthy volunteers and patients.
dose-proportional manner over the dose range studied (5 to 400 mg)
There is no clinically important time- or dose-dependency in the pharmacokinetics of lenalidomide
primary_source.verification: Quotes checked against text extracted from the pinned local PDF (a test repeats this when pypdf is installed).

corroborating_sources.title: REVLIMID (lenalidomide) prescribing information, section 12.3 Pharmacokinetics
corroborating_sources.read_via: https://medlibrary.org/lib/rx/meds/revlimid/page/9/ (mirror; states no revision date). DailyMed and FDA PDF text extraction ended before section 12.3, so the wording was not read from an FDA-hosted copy.
quotes: The single and multiple dose pharmacokinetic disposition of lenalidomide is linear
AUC and Cmax values increasing proportionally with dose.

applies_to: Kim 2026 renal-group check (2.1c): resolves the plan's known difference that dose proportionality was assumed without a source in this repository. Kim's 5-10 mg and the study's 25 mg both lie inside 5-400 mg.
Any comparison that scales exposure between doses for either lenalidomide model.
limits: Population-level linearity; says nothing about an individual.
Does not address whether Fu or clearance change with renal function; that is a separate question.
noted_but_not_used: The same label section reports plasma protein binding of approximately 30% (Fu about 0.7), against Kim's estimated Fu of 0.614. Recorded for a later review of the unbound-to-total conversion; no value is changed.
